title: Small simplicial-presheaf presentations of combinatorial model categories
statement:
Fix universes and infinity-category conventions as in [def-coef-complete-algebroid]. A model category here is complete and cocomplete, with weak equivalences $W$ satisfying two-out-of-three and closure under retracts, and classes $C,F$ such that $(C,F\cap W)$ and $(C\cap W,F)$ are weak factorization systems with functorial factorizations. A weak factorization system consists of mutually characterized left and right diagonal-lifting classes and a factorization of every arrow. Trivial means also in $W$, cofibrant means that the initial map is a cofibration, and fibrant means that the terminal map is a fibration. Combinatorial means locally presentable with both weak factorization systems generated by small sets; locally presentable means generated under $\kappa$-filtered colimits for some regular $\kappa$ by a small set of objects whose ordinary Hom functors preserve these colimits. For every combinatorial model category $\mathcal M$ there exist a small ordinary category $D$, a small set $S$ of arrows in $\mathsf U(D)=\operatorname{Fun}(D^{\mathrm{op}},\mathsf{sSet})$, and a Quillen equivalence
$$L:L_S\mathsf U(D)\rightleftarrows\mathcal M:R.$$
Here $\mathsf{sSet}$ consists of simplicial sets [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-set], with Kan fibrations (right lifting against all horn inclusions), weak homotopy equivalences, and monomorphisms as cofibrations. The projective model structure on $\mathsf U(D)$ has objectwise weak equivalences and fibrations. A simplicial model category is enriched, tensored and cotensored in simplicial sets, with the induced map of mapping spaces for a cofibration and a fibration a Kan fibration, trivial if either input arrow is trivial. The left Bousfield localization $L_S\mathsf U(D)$ has the same cofibrations; its weak equivalences $f$ are precisely the maps for which $\operatorname{Map}^{h}(f,Z)$ is an equivalence of spaces for every projectively fibrant $S$-local $Z$. Here $S$-local means $\operatorname{Map}^{h}(B,Z)\to\operatorname{Map}^{h}(A,Z)$ is an equivalence for every $(A\to B)\in S$, and $\operatorname{Map}^{h}$ is computed by cofibrant replacement of the source and fibrant replacement of the target in the projective model structure. The localized model structure is left proper, combinatorial and simplicial. Left proper means that pushout of a weak equivalence along a cofibration is a weak equivalence. The adjunction $L\dashv R$ preserves cofibrations and trivial cofibrations on the left, and for every cofibrant $A$ in its source and fibrant $Y$ in $\mathcal M$, a map $LA\to Y$ is a weak equivalence if and only if its adjoint $A\to RY$ is a weak equivalence. All sets and presentability conditions are relative to the smaller fixed universe.
